title: Clock-frequency philosophy: self-timed pulsed-global clock distribution
decision: Adopt a self-timed pulsed-global clock design with local clocks generated by pulse generators from a single global clock, rather than a conventional distributed buffered clock tree.
rationale: The paper states that the self-timed approach was chosen to achieve the aggressive cycle-time target and to reduce dependence on a single long global wire, and to limit clock skew/jitter under variation.
outcome: Enables the targeted ~1.3+ GHz cycle time across a large die and supports the chip's variable-frequency operation and power reduction.
weakest_point: Exact cycle-time target number and any quantitative clock-skew claims

title: On-chip L2: shared, inclusive across cores via directory coherence
decision: Use a shared, inclusive on-chip L2 organized as multiple L2 controllers that are address-interleaved and participate in a directory-based MESI coherence protocol.
rationale: Stated reasoning: inclusive sharing reduces coherence traffic between cores and the off-chip L3, and on-chip directory traffic can be handled at the L2 controllers with lower latency than snooping a wide bus.
outcome: L3 acts as off-chip victim cache; latency to off-chip memory is reduced for shared working sets and coherence is scaled to two cores on-die.
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly contrasts inclusive vs exclusive for L2 vs L3

title: Simultaneous multithreading rejected in favor of dual-core chip-level multiprocessing
where_in_paper: Guiding principles / CMP vs SMT discussion
decision: Implement two full processor cores on a single die (CMP), with explicit per-core state, rather than a single wider-issue core that also offers SMT.
alternatives_or_rejected: Adding SMT in addition to (or instead of) the two-core CMP was argued against
rationale: The paper argues that for the commercial workload targets, throughput gains came from replicating complete cores, and that second SMT thread context logic would not fit within the power/area budget that two complete cores required.
outcome: Two single-threaded cores per chip, each appearing as a separate logical processor; future POWER5 added SMT on top of this CMP base.
weakest_point: The paper may describe this as a frequency/cycle-time trade-off rather than as a direct SMT-rejection argument

title: RAS approach: spare/divide logic in the L1 caches and array-repair for larger arrays
decision: Implement per-array redundancy at the L1 caches (divide-by-N spare columns for repair) and ECC plus spare rows for L2 and on-chip arrays, rather than relying solely on bit-level ECC throughout.
alternatives_or_rejected: Using only ECC without redundant spare rows/columns was argued against
rationale: Stated reasoning: L1 caches must support high-frequency accesses that are throughput-sensitive, and it is more area-effective to add repairable spare columns than to increase ECC width enough to mask hard defects in a large array.
outcome: Allows recovery from manufacturing defects in cache arrays without sacrificing normal-mode access time.
weakest_point: Exact terms 'divide' vs 'spare' and which specific arrays are referenced

title: Interconnect: unified on-chip bus between cores, L2 controllers, and external I/O
decision: Use a single on-chip bus structure that concurrently carries address, data, and coherency responses between the two cores, the L2 controllers, and the I/O unit, with logic distributed across the chip.
rationale: The paper argues a unified bus simplifies physical design, supports symmetric core access to L2, and avoids the latency of a separate I/O port to the L2.
outcome: Single interconnect fabric links both cores, the L2, and the chip I/O; addresses are interleaved across the L2 controllers and coherence traffic is also handled through the same fabric.
weakest_point: Whether the paper uses the term 'fabric' or 'bus' and the exact rationale wording
